items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: AI Designs Computer Chips We Can't Understand — But They Seem to Work Really Well
items.summary:
In May 2025, the National Semiconductor Technology Center announced a nearly $10 million award for a Princeton-led effort to develop AI-powered design tools for wireless chips. The programme brought together researchers and industry partners, with Sengupta directing the research.

But just a few months later, the project received a stop-work order. [...] ## AI at the helm

The AI-driven method focused on designing wireless chips, a type of computer chips used for high-frequency applications like 5G networks, radar systems, and advanced sensing technologies. These circuits power innovations in everything from radar systems to autonomous vehicles but their development is notoriously slow. Engineers would start on predefined templates and manually optimize or improve designs through iterative simulations and testing. [...] A A

Edited and reviewed by Zoe Gordon

The AI design features unusual and efficient, circuitry patterns. Credit: Emir Ali Karahan, Princeton University.

Engineers usually design wireless chips using familiar patterns and templates, refining them through simulations and painstaking testing. But a series of studies is proposing a different approach: a deep-learning-enabled design process for creating circuits and components.

items.title: Find My AI Chips: the US Plans to Track GPUs Abroad - IEEE Spectrum
items.summary: To deduce an AI chip’s location, PLV measures the time it takes for a ping to travel from the chip to multiple trusted “landmark” servers around the world and back. Kyle Miller, a senior research analyst at CSET and coauthor of the report, says that for new AI chips, manufacturers could integrate PLV functionality into the hardware itself, while a firmware update could be applied to chips already in circulation. [...] Not all AI chips should be tracked, the researchers note. “The priority should be for the highest-end data center chips—the cream of the crop in high-end data center GPUs,” says Jacob Feldgoise, a senior data research analyst at CSET and coauthor of the report.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. OpenAI retained compatibility with the protocol and client and contributed improvements upstream. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.

items.summary:
🚨ÚLTIMA HORA: OpenAI dice que ha implementado un interruptor de apagado para su investigación de IA de vanguardia.

Llamado Control Room, puede detener los modelos de generar más salida en 35 segundos después de una orden de apagado, incluso si el código del experimento sigue ejecutándose. Los monitores de IA pueden activarlo cuando detectan un comportamiento preocupante.

Si el Control Room en sí falla o es manipulado, todas las solicitudes de inferencia se bloquean por defecto.

Esa protección de fallo cerrado ya está activa en todas las cargas de trabajo de investigación de vanguardia, con el resto programado para seguir en los próximos días. @grok

items.summary:
SoftBank 刚公布上个季度净亏大约 1.1 万亿日元，约合 70 亿美元。一年前同期还赚了 2.5 万亿日元，主要是 OpenAI 持股升值带来的投资收益。

这次亏里有大约 37 亿美元，跟美国 AI 数据中心有关：先付钱锁定设备和产能，项目计划后来改了，钱砸进去却不好回收。财务费用也翻了一倍还多。

它花了约 646 亿美元拿下 OpenAI 大约 13% 的股份，公司股价从六月高点差不多腰斩。看 SoftBank，别只当普通科技股，它更像 AI 投入的放大器：模型故事好的时候利润会很好看，机房和资金成本先落地时，亏也会亏得很响。已发生的账不等于下一步股价怎么走。
